arxiv-2111-04113.title: Stable Lifelong Learning: Spiking neurons as a solution to instability in plastic neural networks
arxiv-2111-04113.creator: Samuel Schmidgall, Joe Hays
arxiv-2111-04113.description: Abstract Synaptic plasticity poses itself as a powerful method of self-regulated unsupervised learning in neural networks. A recent resurgence of interest has developed in utilizing Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) together with synaptic plasticity for intra-lifetime learning. Plasticity has been shown to improve the learning capabilities of these networks in generalizing to novel environmental circumstances.

Google’s Imagen follows this research trend and outperforms DALLE2 as the best model for text-to-image generation.

arxiv-2401-00696.creator: Arindam Das, Yuta Orikasa
arxiv-2401-00696.description: Abstract General U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) extension of the Standard Model (SM) is a well motivated beyond the Standard Model(BSM) scenario where three generations of right handed neutrinos (RHNs) are introduced to cancel gauge and mixed gauge-gravity anomalies.

arxiv-2401-10385.title: Approximation of Solution Operators for High-dimensional PDEs
arxiv-2401-10385.creator: Nathan Gaby, Xiaojing Ye
arxiv-2401-10385.description: Abstract We propose a finite-dimensional control-based method to approximate solution operators for evolutional partial differential equations (PDEs), particularly in high-dimensions. By employing a general reduced-order model, such as a deep neural network, we connect the evolution of the model parameters with trajectories in a corresponding function space.

arxiv-2402-03144.title: Computing Generic Fibers of Polynomial Ideals with FGLM and Hensel Lifting Conference: Proceedings of the 20NN International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation; July XX–YY, 20NN; City, ZZ, USA Proceedings of the 20NN International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation (ISSAC ’
arxiv-2402-03144.creator: Jérémy Berthomieu, Rafael Mohr
arxiv-2402-03144.description: Abstract . We describe a version of the FGLM algorithm that can be used to compute generic fibers of positive-dimensional polynomial ideals. It combines the FGLM algorithm with a Hensel lifting strategy. In analogy with Hensel lifting, we show that this algorithm has a complexity quasi-linear in the number of terms of certain 𝔪 \mathfrak{m} -adic expansions we compute.

arxiv-2508-03330.title: Status and prospects of Muon g-2 experiment
arxiv-2508-03330.description: Abstract This article reviews the muon g-2 experiment, a cornerstone in precision tests of the Standard Model of particle physics. The experiment measures the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon with unprecedented accuracy, seeking potential discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental results that might indicate physics beyond the Standard Model.

arxiv-2509-14872.title: Temporal Representation Learning of Phenotype Trajectories for pCR Prediction in Breast Cancer
arxiv-2509-14872.creator: Ivana Janíčková, Yen Y. Tan, Thomas H. Helbich, Konstantin Miloserdov, Zsuzsanna Bago-Horvath, Ulrike Heber, Georg Langs
arxiv-2509-14872.description: Abstract Effective therapy decisions require models that predict the individual response to treatment. This is challenging since the progression of disease and response to treatment vary substantially across patients. Here, we propose to learn a representation of the early dynamics of treatment response from imaging data to predict pathological complete response (pCR) in breast cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT).

arxiv-2509-18083.title: Reasoning Core: A Scalable RL Environment for LLM Symbolic Reasoning
arxiv-2509-18083.creator: Valentin Lacombe, Valentin Quesnel, Damien Sileo
arxiv-2509-18083.description: Abstract We introduce Reasoning Core, a new scalable environment for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), designed to advance foundational symbolic reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs). Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on games or isolated puzzles, Reasoning Core procedurally generates problems across core formal domains, including PDDL planning, first-order logic, context-free grammar parsing, causal reasoning, and system equation solving.

arxiv-2511-20818.title: Three-dimensional non-relativistic chiral massive higher-spin gravity
arxiv-2511-20818.creator: Arpita Mitra a, Debangshu Mukherjee b, and Tung Tran c
arxiv-2511-20818.description: Abstract We obtain a non-relativistic chiral massive higher-spin gravity in a deformed A ​ d ​ S 3 AdS_{3} spacetime by applying a Lifshitz deformation and subsequent null reduction to chiral massless higher-spin gravity in A ​ d ​ S 4 AdS_{4} .

arxiv-2602-12683.title: Flow Matching from Viewpoint of Proximal Operators
arxiv-2602-12683.creator: Kenji Fukumizu, Wei Huang, Han Bao, Shuntuo Xu, Nisha Chandramoothy
arxiv-2602-12683.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Kenji Fukumizu, Wei Huang, Han Bao, Shuntuo Xu, Nisha Chandramoothy. We reformulate Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM), a class of dynamical generative models, showing that it admits an exact proximal formulation via an extended Brenier potential, without assuming that the target distribution has a density. In particular, the mapping to recover the target point is exactly given by a proximal operator, which yields an explicit proximal expression of the vector field.

pmc-10573241.title: Flowability and Strength Characteristics of Binary Cementitious Systems Containing Silica Fume, Fly Ash, Metakaolin, and Glass Cullet Powder
pmc-10573241.creator: Mohammad Iqbal Khan, Yassir M Abbas, Galal Fares, Fahad K Alqahtani, Valentin Antonovič, Jurgita Malaiškienė
pmc-10573241.description: The present study examines the effects of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) on the flowability and strength development of binary mixes. This study was primarily motivated by the need to bridge the knowledge gap regarding paste and mortar mixes containing binary cement from a variety of performance perspectives.

pmc-11517703.title: How to improve the inclusion of the elderly in the local community for better mental health?
pmc-11517703.creator: O Stanojevic-Jerkovic, S Oreski
pmc-11517703.description: Issue/problemSocial exclusion, ageism and low health/digital literacy intertwine with growing trends in mental disorders, including abuse in Slovenian elderly. To cope with these issues, besides rising competencies, there is a need for stable and continuous partnerships of all relevant stakeholders in the local communities.

pmc-11709412.title: The involvement of human CD33 in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease mouse model
pmc-11709412.creator: Tzu‐Ching Su, Wei‐Chien Hung, Irene Han‐Juo Cheng
pmc-11709412.description: BackgroundGenome‐wide association studies demonstrated that immune suppressive receptor CD33 variants are associated with high susceptibility to developing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Human CD33 (hCD33) regulates microglial immune response and clearance ability. However, the differential regulation of phagocytosis by human and mouse CD33 imposes constraints on utilizing the mouse model for investigating the role of CD33 in AD.

pmc-12543499.title: Circulation and Genetic Characterizations of Coronaviruses From Companion Animals in Chengdu, Southwest China: One-Year Postpandemic
pmc-12543499.creator: Linxuan Liao, Shanshan Wu, Yihang Xu, Mengxi Cao, Xiao Zhang, Liying Yi, Baochao Zhang, Jiayi Chen, Xin Xu, Xiaofang Pei
pmc-12543499.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Coronaviruses (CoVs) can cross species barriers and endanger public health. Despite reports on their circulation and evolution in companion animals during the pandemic, postpandemic surveillance remains crucial. Therefore, during the first postpandemic year, 309 samples from 263 companion animals (cats and dogs) in Chengdu, China, were detected for CoVs using a universal assay based on Rdrp genes combined with one-generation sequencing.

pmc-13203042.title: A synopsis of competence-regulated virulence in Streptococcus pneumoniae
pmc-13203042.creator: Sook Yin Chong, Shi Qian Lew, Gee W Lau
pmc-13203042.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) remains a significant cause of pneumonia, bacteremia, sepsis, meningitis, and otitis media. The ability of pneumococcus to enter a state of genetic competence is central to pneumococcal adaptability and virulence. Activation of the competence state enables pneumococcus to uptake exogenous DNA for genetic transformation, acquire genome plasticity and antimicrobial resistance, while also regulating stress tolerance, biofilm formation, and coordinated expression of virulence factors.

pmc-13361221.title: Visualization of G3BP1–RNA Condensate Nascent Assembly and Early Maturation by HS-AFM
pmc-13361221.creator: S. M. Neaz Mahmud, Noriyuki Kodera, Hanae Sato
pmc-13361221.description: Stress granules (SGs) are stress-induced ribonucleoprotein condensates assembled around untranslated mRNAs and RNA-binding proteins. G3BP1 is a central regulator of SG formation, yet the molecular events that initiate G3BP1-mediated condensation remain poorly understood. Current models propose that condensation is initiated by RNA–RNA interactions, G3BP1 self-association, or RNA-dependent assembly of G3BP1 into higher-order networks.

pmc-13445749.title: Negative social interpretation bias and suicidality: Indirect pathways through social anxiety and perceived burdensomeness
pmc-13445749.creator: Hannah C. Hamrick, Arooj Abid, Christopher G. Guadalupe, Nathan M. Hager, Morgan S. Middlebrooks, Matt R. Judah
pmc-13445749.description: BackgroundSocial anxiety has been linked to suicidality through thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness, consistent with the interpersonal psychological theory of suicide. Broader underlying cognitive vulnerabilities, such as biased perceptions of social situations, may also play a role. This study examined whether negative social interpretation bias predicted suicidality via social anxiety symptoms and unmet interpersonal needs (i.e.

pmc-13473151.title: Facile and cost-effective synthesis and characterization of hormone stabilized biocompatible gold nanoparticles for biomedical applications
pmc-13473151.creator: Rajendran Ganapathy, Murugadas Anbazhagan, Punitha Natarajan, Ancy Jenifer Albin, Nallusamy Duraisamy, Kathiravan Krishnan, Gholamreza Abdi, Maryam Abbasi Tarighat
pmc-13473151.description: Metal nanoparticles possess unique characteristic features suitable for biomedical and other biological applications such as antimicrobial activity to drug delivery. Non-toxic, biocompatible nanoparticles are essential for these applications. Many of previously described methods applied heat or boiling and toxic chemicals like SDS, beta mercaptoethanol, EDTA, sodium citrate for nanoparticles synthesis.

pmc-13526644.title: Patient‐Specific Computational Fluid Dynamics Modeling of Airway Collapse in Infants With Robin Sequence
pmc-13526644.creator: Gautam Jalori, Michael Barbour, Michael Bindschadler, Kelly Evans, Jake Dahl, Alberto Aliseda
pmc-13526644.description: Robin Sequence (RS) is a congenital condition in which patients experience dynamic, periodic obstruction or collapse of the upper airway due to an underdeveloped jaw and a posteriorly displaced tongue. Current clinical techniques for evaluating airway obstruction do not provide quantifiable data and fail to account for the dynamic nature of obstruction or collapse.

pmc-13589544.title: The EAR motif-containing adaptor protein ECAP enhances ABI5-mediated ABA signaling to inhibit seed germination in Arabidopsis
pmc-13589544.creator: Xing Li, Jian Zhang, Chenming Xu, Lili Wang, Shunping Yan
pmc-13589544.description: The phytohormone abscisic acid (ABA) regulates diverse biological processes, including seed germination, in which the transcription factor abscisic acid insensitive 5 (ABI5) plays an essential role. Here, we show that the EAR motif-containing adaptor protein (ECAP) functions as a positive regulator of ABI5 to inhibit seed germination in Arabidopsis.

pmc-13632020.title: Impact of COVID-19 on TB and HIV/AIDS severity in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review
pmc-13632020.creator: Endawoke Amsalu, Melese Yeshambaw, Dagim Jirata
pmc-13632020.description: BackgroundBeyond its profound health, social, and economic consequences, COVID-19 poses a serious threat to the management of tuberculosis (TB) and HIV/AIDS. However, empirical evidence remains limited. This study evaluates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on TB and HIV/AIDS service delivery across low- and middle-income countries.MethodsThis systematic review protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42021266242).

pmc-13637346.title: The impact of community paramedicine service on prehospital time intervals in rural Norway: a quasi-experimental study
pmc-13637346.creator: Odd Eirik Elden, Oddvar Uleberg, Emma Brulin, Bodil J. Landstad, Maja Pålsdatter Lønvik, Øyvind Salvesen, Havard Dalen
pmc-13637346.description: BackgroundCommunity paramedicine service (CPS) may improve prehospital healthcare delivery in rural regions. As CPS does not provide patient transport, its introduction could prolong prehospital time intervals. Thus, we aimed to evaluate whether CPS implementation influenced prehospital time intervals for acute patients admitted to hospital.

pmc-13672172.title: Scalable Emitter Photonic Integrated Circuits on an Open‐Access Indium Phosphide Foundry
pmc-13672172.creator: Durvasa Y. Gupta, Axel Schoenau, Hendrik Boerma, Shahram Keyvaninia, Patrick Runge
pmc-13672172.description: We present an easy access prototype solution using Fraunhofer‐HHI's open‐access indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits (PIC) platform. The process design kit enabled generic multiproject wafer process co‐integrates low‐loss passive components with gain, modulation, and detection. A high‐speed 80 GBaud traveling‐wave Mach–Zehnder modulator (MZM) is a key building block for emitter PICs.
